Water impoundments for livestock would be limited in size and would have very little value for recreation or aquatic habitat. Also, competition would exist between some wildlife species and livestock, so wildlife populations would be reduced. Finally, removal of protective vegetative cover by grazing would cause increased erosion. Livestock would also trample vegetation and compact the soil surface.
Cropland
Approximately 12% of the land on the tracts is now being farmed, or has been farmed in the past. There is additional land which could be farmed, but most of these areas are too small to justify large-scale farming efforts. Historically, highly productive vegetable gardens were raised around many ranchsteads, and in general the bottomlands are quite fertile.
Current Montana State law requires reclamation to self-sustaining native grassland prior to release of reclamation bonding. This requirement works to ensure that the land is restored to a condition which is capable of supporting stable vegetative growth, and does not limit the post-reclamation uses of the land. After the company's bond is released, the land can be sold or otherwise transfered to non-grassland uses.
